summary: The Rijksmuseum describes an online Comparator that places artworks side by side and lets visitors zoom into details.
audience: Proposed audience of English-reading art learners who already browse museum collections for visual references.
market: Proposed international English-language audience for online museum discovery. The campaign points to the museum’s English collection information page.
peer_rationale: The Louvre offers another online collection for people exploring artworks. This comparison concerns audience attention and collection discovery.

source.quote: Use the Comparator to place artworks side by side and zoom in on the smallest details.
source.scope: The museum describes side-by-side comparison and zoom in Collection Online.

peer_source.quote: The Collections database consists of entries for more than 500,000 works
peer_source.scope: The published database covers works from Musée du Louvre and Musée National Eugène-Delacroix. It provides peer context for online collection discovery.

objective: Increase clicks from a collection discovery post to the Rijksmuseum page that explains the Comparator.
metric: Outbound click-through rate to the collection information page, measured as clicks divided by post impressions.
assumption: We expect a specific visual comparison task to interest art learners. Audience size, baseline click-through rate and demand for the tool require measurement.

alternatives.name: Side-by-side study
alternatives.plan: Lead with one practical task and direct readers to the Comparator explanation.
alternatives.tradeoff: A concrete reason to visit, with a learning step between the post and the tool.

alternatives.name: Zoom into a detail
alternatives.plan: Lead with close looking and invite readers to see the tool that makes detail study possible.
alternatives.tradeoff: A visually direct message with less emphasis on how two works relate.

alternatives.name: A looking exercise
alternatives.plan: Offer a prompt about what changes when readers compare artworks.
alternatives.tradeoff: Invites curiosity and needs editorial guidance for selecting works.

strategy_reason: Side-by-side study matches the published Comparator feature and gives readers one action. If analytics show visits with little follow-through, test the close-looking message.

directions.name: Detail study
directions.rationale: An alternate hook tests interest in close looking before the selected side-by-side message. Rounded shapes suggest magnification.
directions.headline: Look a little closer.
directions.message: Zoom into artwork details with the Rijksmuseum Comparator.
directions.caption: Start with a detail. Collection Online describes how the Rijksmuseum Comparator lets you zoom in and put artworks side by side. Read how it works.
directions.hook: What changes when you look closer?
directions.shot: A crop marker tightens around an abstract coloured shape.
directions.middle_shot: Keep the first panel in view as the second panel shows an enlarged detail of the same abstract shape.
directions.end_shot: End with Rijksmuseum and the words “See how it works.”

directions.name: Side-by-side looking
directions.rationale: Overlapping gallery-like frames suggest putting different works in view together.
directions.headline: See two artworks side by side.
directions.message: Compare artworks in Rijksmuseum Collection Online.
directions.caption: Try a different way of looking. The Rijksmuseum Comparator places artworks side by side. Start with the Collection Online guide.
directions.shot: Show two empty gallery frames entering from opposite sides.
directions.middle_shot: Show the frames aligned at the same height. Introduce the name Comparator over the space between them.
directions.end_shot: Hold the Rijksmuseum name and the call to action “Read about the Comparator.”

directions.name: One looking question
directions.rationale: A question invites readers to compare what catches their eye first.
directions.headline: What catches your eye first?
directions.message: Put artworks side by side with the Rijksmuseum Comparator.
directions.caption: Pick a detail to notice first, then look again with a second artwork alongside. The Collection Online guide explains how the Comparator works.
directions.shot: A dot highlights the edge of one abstract gallery shape.
directions.middle_shot: Move the dot into a second frame and leave both frames visible for the comparison.
directions.end_shot: Hold the Rijksmuseum name and invite viewers to read about the tool.

human_review: Confirm the Comparator link and the steps from the information page on mobile before launch.
Clear institutional name and branding use with the museum. If a future version includes artwork, verify its individual asset rights.
Check whether a distinct outbound event for the Comparator can be measured before comparing campaign variants.
